items.headline: Nvidia's board reverses its CEO decision, reinstating the former chief less than two weeks after his resignation; shares opened about 30% higher on Nov 23
items.why: Leadership uncertainty at the largest AI-chip supplier was a live overhang on the whole AI trade, and the board's reversal removes it, though the stock then gave back much of the move within two sessions.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Nvidia reverses course and brings its CEO back

items.headline: AI and chip stocks sell off again on Nov 25: AMD, Micron, Marvell and Intel each fell more than 9% intraday, Nvidia closed down 3.91% at $149.30 for a second straight loss
items.why: The reinstatement bounce was erased in two sessions, which says the market is trading AI-demand and rate risk rather than company governance.

items.headline: Analysis flags tighter AI-chip export controls and more scrutiny of AI chip sales as the next major risk for Nvidia
items.why: Policy, not demand, is the variable that can cap AI-chip revenue from here, so any new licensing rule moves the whole semiconductor group.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs lose about $570M on Nov 23, a fifth straight day of outflows; November outflows hit a record of roughly $4.7B to $4.9B depending on the data provider
items.why: Persistent ETF redemptions are the main identifiable source of selling pressure, and the month is already the worst on record for the product.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips to about $58,600 after briefly topping $64,000 on Nov 23; down nearly 30% in a month and more than half from the October 2025 high near $126,000
items.why: The failed push above $64,000 and the break back under $60,000 show rallies are being sold, with last week's two-year low (under $55,500) now the next reference.

items.headline: On-chain data shows large wallets took about 10,000 BTC off exchanges in November while ETFs sold about 70,000 BTC; cumulative ETF net inflows remain near $52B, about 83% of the October 2025 peak
items.why: Most of the capital that came in via ETFs is still in place, so this reads as partial unwinding rather than a full exit, though ETF selling is outpacing wallet buying about seven to one.

items.headline: October core PCE inflation runs 3.3% year on year versus 3.2% expected, headline 3.8%; Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3%; futures price a 25bp Fed hike on Dec 8-9 at roughly 96% to 98%
items.why: Hotter inflation plus strong growth removes any case for easing and makes a December hike the base case, which is what is pressuring long-duration assets across the board.

items.headline: US announces proposed tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other partners after a Section 301 probe; semiconductors, autos, steel and aluminum excluded; the US-China truce expires Jan 10
items.why: A new tariff layer on top of 3.3% core inflation raises the odds that price pressure persists into 2027, and the Jan 10 truce deadline is the next hard date for US-China trade risk.

items.headline: Gulf supply risk escalates: Saudi forces intercept four drones aimed at Ras Tanura, Iran steps up attacks on Hormuz shipping, and Brent jumps 3.5% to $94.61
items.why: Attacks on export infrastructure and the main shipping chokepoint are what move crude, and higher oil feeds directly into the inflation problem the Fed is already hiking against.
